name: Friday
tagline: Your desktop AI copilot for everyday tasks.
description: Friday is a desktop application that puts a capable, personal AI assistant on your computer. You chat with it in plain language, and it gets real work done: it reads and writes files, searches the web, generates images, transcribes your voice, speaks back, runs on a schedule, and connects to the tools and messaging apps you already use.
intro: Unlike a website chatbot, Friday runs as a native app on your machine. You bring your own AI provider keys, your data and credentials stay local, and every action that touches your files, accounts, or the outside world passes through explicit permission checks.

tableOfContents.label: How a request flows through Friday

whatFridayIs.title: What Friday is
whatFridayIs.body: Friday is a native desktop app for Windows, macOS, and Linux built on Electron. At its core is an AI agent: not just a chat window, but an assistant that can take actions on your behalf using a set of tools. You describe a goal in natural language, and Friday plans, uses the right tools, and returns a concrete result: a written file, an answer with sources, a generated image, a scheduled job, a transcribed recording, and more.
whatFridayIs.closing: You stay in control. Friday works with the AI providers you choose and pay for, keeps its working data on your own machine, and asks for permission before doing anything sensitive.

audiences: Anyone who wants a personal AI assistant that lives on their desktop instead of a browser tab.
Professionals and power users who want the AI to actually do things: manage files, draft documents, automate recurring tasks, and pull from their email, calendar, and cloud storage.
People who care about privacy and prefer to use their own AI provider accounts and keep data local.
Tinkerers and teams who want to extend the assistant with custom skills, tool servers, and messaging integrations.

keyIdeas.title: Chat that acts.
keyIdeas.description: Talk to Friday like a person; it uses tools to complete the task, not just describe it.

keyIdeas.title: Bring your own AI.
keyIdeas.description: Plug in your own API keys for the model providers you prefer. Friday is not locked to a single vendor.

keyIdeas.title: Local first.
keyIdeas.description: The app, your settings, credentials, and conversation history live on your device.

keyIdeas.title: Permissioned.
keyIdeas.description: Writing files, sending messages, or accessing private data requires explicit approval.

keyIdeas.title: Extensible.
keyIdeas.description: Add skills, connect external tools via MCP, and reach the assistant from your favorite chat apps.

keyIdeas.title: Automatable.
keyIdeas.description: Schedule the assistant to run jobs on a recurring basis, and run periodic health checks.

features.title: The AI assistant (chat)
features.body: The heart of Friday is a conversational assistant. You type or speak a request, and it responds in a clean, readable chat with full Markdown, syntax-highlighted code blocks, and inline images.
items: It takes action. When a task needs it, the assistant reaches for tools to read files, search the web, generate an image, and more, then weaves the results into its answer.
Transparent tool activity. You can see what the assistant is doing, grouped by tool, as it works.
Permission prompts. When an action is sensitive, Friday shows a confirmation card so you approve before it happens.
Natural, direct tone. The assistant is tuned to sound human and practical, brief for quick questions and more careful for complex work.
Session history. Conversations are saved locally so you can revisit or clear them.

features.title: Agent tools
features.body: Tools are the assistant's hands. Depending on your setup, Friday can read, write, edit, patch, run commands, search the web, fetch pages, drive a browser, generate images, schedule jobs, load skills, spin up subagents, and use tools exposed by connected MCP servers.

tools.name: Read / write / edit files
tools.description: Open, create, and modify files in your workspace, with safety checks and approval prompts before changes.

tools.name: Apply patch
tools.description: Make precise, surgical edits to existing files.

tools.name: Run commands & processes
tools.description: Execute shell commands and longer-running processes to build, test, or automate work.

tools.name: Web search
tools.description: Look things up on the internet for fresh, accurate information.

tools.name: Web fetch
tools.description: Pull the contents of a specific page or URL.

tools.name: Web browser
tools.description: Drive a real browser to interact with web pages when a simple fetch isn't enough.

tools.name: Create image
tools.description: Generate images from a text description.

tools.name: Schedule (cron)
tools.description: Create, update, pause, resume, list, and run scheduled jobs.

tools.name: Load skills
tools.description: Pull in a reusable skill to handle a class of work.

tools.name: Subagents
tools.description: Spin up focused helper agents for independent parts of a larger task.

tools.name: MCP tools
tools.description: Use any tool exposed by a connected MCP server.

features.closing: The assistant uses tools only when they improve the result, and treats their output as evidence rather than instructions. It won't send messages, change records, delete data, or touch production systems without clear authorization.

features.title: Voice: dictation and read-aloud
items: Speech-to-text transcription lets you talk instead of type, with support for real-time dictation as you speak.
Text-to-speech lets the assistant read its replies aloud in a natural voice.
You choose which provider and voice model powers each direction, and grant microphone permission on your own terms.

features.title: Image generation
features.body: Describe an image in words and Friday creates it, using the image provider and model you select. Generated images appear directly in the conversation and can be saved. This is exposed both as a chat tool and as its own dedicated image workspace in settings.

features.title: Providers: bring your own AI
features.body: Friday doesn't ship a single built-in model. Instead, you connect the AI providers you want to use by adding your own API keys. Each capability can use a different provider and model, so you can mix and match for quality, cost, and speed.
items: Assistant: the chat/agent brain.
Speech-to-Text: transcription of your voice.
Text-to-Speech: the assistant's spoken voice.
Text-to-Image: image generation.
Text-to-Video: coming soon.
Music / Audio: coming soon.
features.closing: Provider adapters normalize many different vendors into one consistent interface, including OpenAI-compatible providers. API keys are stored as credentials in local settings and are never displayed back in plain text once saved.

features.title: Skills
features.body: Skills are reusable capabilities that teach Friday how to handle a particular kind of work, so it doesn't have to rediscover the same workflow every time. A skill can bundle instructions, reference material, templates, schemas, and optional executable behavior.
items: Install and manage example skills or download more into your personal skill library, then enable or disable each one.
Automatic discovery selects relevant enabled skills before answering.
Skills run within declared limits, and unsafe or disabled skills are blocked with an audit of why a skill was chosen or rejected.

features.title: Connectors
features.body: Connectors link Friday to the external services where your work lives, so the assistant can act on your email, calendar, files, and workspaces.
items: Google: Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive.
Microsoft: Outlook email, Outlook calendar, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams.
Dropbox: file storage.
features.closing: Connectors are powered by MCP. Secrets are referenced securely rather than pasted into plain records, and actions that read private data or make changes go through Friday's permission checks.

features.title: MCP servers
features.body: Friday supports the Model Context Protocol, an open standard for giving AI assistants access to external tools and data.
items: Remote MCP servers: hosted tool servers reached over HTTP, with optional token/key auth.
Local stdio MCP servers: tools that run as a local process on your machine.
features.closing: Once connected, the tools that server provides become available to the assistant automatically.

features.title: Channels: chat from anywhere
features.body: Channels let you talk to Friday from outside the app, through the messaging platforms you already use. A message arrives from a channel, Friday runs an agent turn, and the reply is delivered back through the same channel.
items: Live today: Telegram.
Catalog ready: Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams, WhatsApp, Signal, Matrix, Mattermost, Google Chat, LINE, IRC, Twitch, and more.
Access control: each channel has its own configuration, enabled state, direct-message policy, and securely stored secrets.

features.title: Task scheduler
features.body: Friday can work on a schedule, even when you're not actively chatting. The task scheduler lets you set up recurring jobs, a daily summary, a periodic check, a routine cleanup, and have the assistant run them automatically.
items: Create, update, pause, resume, list, and run schedules on demand.
Each schedule runs an agent turn with its own instructions, using the provider and model you choose for scheduled work.

features.title: Health checks
features.body: The health feature runs the assistant on a periodic interval against a checklist you define, so Friday can proactively verify that things are in order and report back. You set the interval, the provider/model, and the checklist instructions that describe what healthy means for your setup.

features.title: Memory and personalization
features.body: Friday builds up a personal working context so it gets more useful over time.
items: Memory: durable facts and preferences the assistant should remember across conversations.
User profile and identity: who you are and how you like the assistant to behave.
Workspace: a local working area where the assistant keeps and edits the files it produces.
features.closing: This personalization stays on your device and shapes how the assistant responds and acts.

requestFlow: You make a request in chat, typed or spoken.
Friday understands the goal, constraints, and expected output. If something critical is ambiguous, it asks a focused question; otherwise it proceeds with a reasonable, reversible assumption.
It plans and picks tools, skills, connectors, or subagents.
It acts, with permission. Sensitive actions prompt you for approval first.
It verifies and responds with a concrete, ready-to-use answer or artifact.
It remembers what matters and, if scheduled, can repeat the work automatically later.
privacySecurity: Local by default. The app, your settings, provider keys, connector credentials, and conversation history live on your own machine.
Bring your own keys. You use your own AI provider accounts; Friday doesn't put a vendor in between.
Secrets stay secret. API keys and channel/connector credentials are stored as credentials and are not shown in plain text after saving, not logged, and not rendered.
Explicit permissions. Any tool or connector action that writes, deletes, publishes, or reads private data must pass a permission check.
Hardened app shell. The user interface runs in a locked-down, sandboxed environment with strict isolation from the underlying system, and browser windows are created through safe defaults.
privacyNote: Friday does not currently claim any formal regulated-data certification. Review your own AI providers' and connected services' terms for how they handle data you send them.
platformsLanguages: Platforms: Windows, macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon), and Linux.
Interface languages: English and Italian, with a language switcher in settings.
Appearance: Light, dark, and system themes.
Convenience: A command menu for quick navigation, plus optional menu-bar/tray presence.
gettingStarted: Install and open Friday on your computer.
Add a provider key in Settings -> Providers.
Pick which provider and model powers the assistant, and optionally transcription, voice, and image generation.
Start chatting and approve any permission prompts for actions that touch your files or accounts.
Extend it by enabling skills, connecting Google/Microsoft/Dropbox accounts, adding MCP tool servers, linking Telegram, or scheduling a recurring task.

glossary.definition: The AI that chats with you and takes actions using tools.
An AI vendor, accessed with your API key, that powers a capability like chat, transcription, speech, or images.
A capability slot such as Assistant, Speech-to-Text, Text-to-Speech, or Text-to-Image that you assign a provider and model to.
A specific action the assistant can perform, such as reading a file or searching the web.
A reusable, packaged workflow that teaches Friday how to handle a class of tasks.
A link to an external service so the assistant can work with your email, calendar, and files.
An open standard for connecting external tools and data to the assistant.
A messaging platform you can use to reach Friday from outside the app.
Recurring jobs that run the assistant automatically.
A periodic, checklist-driven run that verifies your setup and reports back.
